_meta.title: Drosophila chemoreceptor responses, gustatory dose-response, internal-state modulation, and connectome GRN type mapping
_meta.confidence_scale: high = verified in fetched primary/database; medium = verified secondary/abstract or single study; low = snippet/unclear; ESTIMATE/DERIVED = our own estimate or calculation
_meta.connectome_note: ORN types named ORN_<glomerulus> in hemibrain/FlyWire; check VC3/VC5/VM6 renaming (see olfactory.connectome_naming).

Or1a.note: LARVAL-ONLY receptor (DoOR adult=FALSE): ignore for adult fly model

Or22a.note: DM2; Or22a/Or22b co-expressed; broad ester receptor (ethyl hexanoate, isoamyl acetate)

Or22c.note: LARVAL-ONLY receptor (DoOR adult=FALSE): ignore for adult fly model

Or24a.note: LARVAL-ONLY receptor (DoOR adult=FALSE): ignore for adult fly model

Or30a.note: LARVAL-ONLY receptor (DoOR adult=FALSE): ignore for adult fly model

Or33a.note: DoOR assigns to ab4B/DA2 (with Or56a). Geosmin receptor is Or56a (Stensmyr 2012); DoOR column ab4B carries the geosmin response

Or35a.note: VC3 (hemibrain v1.2 name: VC3l). Coexpresses Ir76b; alcohols/hexanol/hexanal

Or42b.note: vinegar/ethyl acetate high-affinity ester receptor; required for vinegar attraction (Semmelhack & Wang 2009); sNPF facilitation in hunger (Root 2011)

Or45a.note: LARVAL-ONLY receptor (DoOR adult=FALSE): ignore for adult fly model

Or45b.note: LARVAL-ONLY receptor (DoOR adult=FALSE): ignore for adult fly model

Or47b.note: VA1v; fly odors/pheromone (male courtship), not food

Or59a.note: LARVAL-ONLY receptor (DoOR adult=FALSE): ignore for adult fly model

Or74a.note: LARVAL-ONLY receptor (DoOR adult=FALSE): ignore for adult fly model

Or85a.note: DM5; recruited at high vinegar concentration -> reduced attraction; tachykinin suppression in hunger (Ko 2015). Shares ab2B with Or33b

Or85c.note: LARVAL-ONLY receptor (DoOR adult=FALSE): ignore for adult fly model

Or92a.note: diacetyl (2,3-butanedione); contributes to vinegar attraction (Semmelhack & Wang 2009)

Or94a.note: LARVAL-ONLY receptor (DoOR adult=FALSE): ignore for adult fly model

Or94b.note: LARVAL-ONLY receptor (DoOR adult=FALSE): ignore for adult fly model

Or69a.note: D; Or69aA food odors + Or69aB (Z)-4-undecenal pheromone (Lebreton 2017)

Ir75a.note: DP1l (NOT DL2); acetic, propionic acid, diacetyl (Silbering 2011; Prieto-Godino 2016)

Ir64a.DC4.note: DC4; proton/acid-specific (Ai 2010); needed for acetic acid avoidance and >5% CO2 (carbonic acid) avoidance

Or56a.note: geosmin-specific (Stensmyr 2012 Cell 151:1345); DoOR data under column ab4B

Rh50/Amt.note: ammonia (ac1 Rh50+; sacculus). Hemibrain v1.2 name for VM6 was VC5 (Task et al. 2022 eLife 11:e72599)

connectome_naming.renaming: Schlegel P et al. 2021 eLife 10:e66018 and Task D et al. 2022 eLife 11:e72599 renamed: VC3l -> VC3 (Or35a), VC3m -> VC5 (Ir41a), old VC5 -> VM6 (Rh50/ammonia). Hemibrain v1.2 neuPrint type strings may still use VC3l/VC3m/VC5-old; FlyWire (Schlegel 2024 Nature) uses the new names.
connectome_naming.VM6_split: VM6v (ac1, Rh50+Ir25a), VM6m and VM6l (sacculus, Ir8a+) at ORN level only (Task 2022).
connectome_naming.thermo_hygro: VP1d/VP1l/VP1m (Ir21a/Ir40a/Ir93a/Ir68a), VP2 (Gr28b.d hot), VP3, VP4, VP5 are not olfactory.
corrections_to_brief: Ir75a -> DP1l (not DL2; DL2d/DL2v are Ir75b/Ir75c)
Or83c -> DC3 (not VA6; VA6 is Or82a)
Or85a -> DM5 shares ab2B with Or33b; Or47a -> DM3 shares ab5B with Or33b
connectome_naming.total_glomeruli: 58 in hemibrain antennal lobe (incl. VP thermo/hygro)

door_consensus._source: DoOR 2.0 (Muench D & Galizia CG 2016 Sci Rep 6:21841, doi:10.1038/srep21841). Data package ropensci/DoOR.data (GitHub), files door_response_matrix.csv, door_mappings.csv, odor.csv; raw base URL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ropensci/DoOR.data/master/data/
door_consensus._values: consensus_raw = door_response_matrix (globally normalized 0..1, includes spontaneous firing rate SFR). consensus_sfr_reset = value - SFR row (DoOR resetSFR convention: 0 = spontaneous, negative = inhibition). Only receptors with data for that odorant are listed; absence = untested, not zero.
_caveats: DoOR consensus is unitless and normalized per receptor then globally; cross-receptor comparisons are approximate.
Ir columns (Ir64a.DC4, Ir75a, ...) come mostly from calcium imaging (Silbering 2011) and a few odorants; a 1.0 for Ir64a.DC4 means best of few tested.
Or85c, Or45a, Or45b, Or30a, Or1a, Or22c, Or24a, Or59a, Or74a, Or94a, Or94b are larval-only.
ac1, ac2, ac3_noOr35a, ac4 = whole-sensillum coeloconic recordings (multiple neuron types).
Hallem 2006 at 1e-2 is a saturating concentration for many best ligands; use dose-response section for low concentrations.

hallem2006_spikes._source: Hallem EA & Carlson JR 2006 Cell 125:143, doi:10.1016/j.cell.2006.01.050 (24 ORs in the empty-neuron ab3A system, 110 odorants at 1e-2 dilution; acids, alcohols methanol/ethanol, acetaldehyde, lactic acid, ammonia etc. diluted in water, others in paraffin oil). Values extracted from DoOR.data per-receptor CSVs column Hallem.2006.EN.
hallem2006_spikes._units: net_spikes_s = odor-evoked change from spontaneous rate (as published; verified identical to the Hallem 2006 columns reproduced in Knaden et al. 2012 Cell Rep Table S1). IMPORTANT: DoOR.data column Hallem.2006.EN stores ABSOLUTE rates (net + spontaneous), despite its metadata; we subtracted the SFR row. absolute_rate = net + spontaneous. Values below ~30-50 spikes/s are weak (Hallem & Carlson used >=50 as a response criterion). Or42b, Or92a (not functional in empty neuron) and Ir/Gr receptors are not in this dataset.

ionotropic_and_CO2._note: Ionotropic receptor (IR) and CO2 ORNs relevant to fermentation odors.

entries.ligands: DC4: acids/protons (acetic, propionic, butyric, phenylacetic, HCl, high CO2 via carbonic acid); DP1m: organic acids, diacetyl
phenylacetic acid, phenylacetaldehyde (Silbering 2011; Grosjean Y et al. 2011 Nature 478:236)
polyamines (putrescine, cadaverine; Hussain A et al. 2016 PLoS Biol 14:e1002455)
CO2 (inhibited by 1-hexanol, 2,3-butanedione in some studies; DoOR Kwon 2007 WT shows -31 spikes/s to 1-hexanol)
entries.valence: aversive at rest; flying/active flies attracted to CO2 via Ir25a (van Breugel 2018)

ionotropic_and_CO2.source: Silbering 2011 J Neurosci 31:13357; Ai 2010 Nature 468:691; Task D et al. 2022 eLife 11:e72599; DoOR mappings

dose_response._note: Hill form R = Rmax * C^n/(C^n + EC50^n) (+ spontaneous). Dilution = v/v in paraffin oil (or water for acids) in the odor cartridge; vapor concentration at the fly is roughly 1e-3 to 1e-2 x saturated headspace for typical delivery (see conversion). Values marked ESTIMATE are our defaults, not published fits.

Si2019_larva.EC50_distribution: power law P(x) ~ x^(-lambda-1), lambda = 0.42; EC50s span several orders of magnitude
Si2019_larva.source: Si G, Kanwal JK, Hu Y, ... Samuel ADT 2019 Neuron 101:950, doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2018.12.030

Hallem2006_Kreher2008_fraction_respondin.source: Kreher SA, Mathew D, Kim J, Carlson JR 2008 Neuron 59:110, doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2008.06.010 (larval ORs in empty neuron)

max_rates.source: Olsen SR, Bhandawat V, Wilson RI 2010 Neuron 66:287 doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2010.04.009

receptor_specific.interpretation: values = -log10(EC50 dilution) from calcium imaging (antenna = ORN terminals imaged at antenna? / AL = antennal lobe). e.g. isoamyl acetate EC50 ~1e-4 dilution. Interpretation of DoOR column semantics as -log10 EC50 is ours; verify against Pelz 2006.
receptor_specific.source: Pelz D, Roeske T, Syed Z, de Bruyne M, Galizia CG 2006 J Neurobiol 66:1544, doi:10.1002/neu.20333; extracted from DoOR.data columns Pelz.2006.AntEC50 / Pelz.2006.ALEC50 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ropensci/DoOR.data/master/data/Or22a.csv)
Hallem & Carlson 2006 Cell 125:143 (net = DoOR Hallem.2006.EN minus SFR 4; matches Knaden 2012 Table S1)

receptor_specific.note_units: DoOR per-study values; whether spontaneous rate (~9 spikes/s for ab1A) is included varies by study

EC50_ESTIMATE.basis: Kreher 2008 larval Or42b is the high-affinity ethyl acetate receptor (half-max below Or42a threshold; EC50 roughly 1e-7-1e-6, value from figure not extracted); adult ab1A saturates (~250 spikes/s) by 1e-2. ESTIMATE.

receptor_specific.source: DoOR.data Or42b.csv (de Bruyne 2001 Neuron 30:537; Dobritsa 2003 Neuron 37:827; de Bruyne 2010 Chem Senses; Marshall 2010); Kreher 2008 Neuron 59:110

receptor_specific.note: low-affinity partner of Or42b in larva; needed at high ethyl acetate concentrations (Kreher 2008)

EC50_ESTIMATE.basis: not found; ESTIMATE by analogy to other best-ligand pairs (Si 2019 distribution)

receptor_specific.facts: DC4 activated by 1% acetic acid and 3.6% HCl; response scales inversely with pH (sodium acetate series) = proton detector. DP1m broader organic acids, not pH. Ir8a co-receptor required. Behavior: T-maze 10 uL of 10% acetic acid aversive.

EC50_ESTIMATE.basis: responses reported at 1%; no dose-response fit found. ESTIMATE

receptor_specific.source: Ai M et al. 2010 Nature 468:691 doi:10.1038/nature09537; Ai M et al. 2013 J Neurosci 33:10741 doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.5419-12.2013; Silbering AF et al. 2011 J Neurosci 31:13357 doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.2360-11.2011 (DoOR Silbering.2011.AL_8a, dF/F %)

receptor_specific.facts: robust responses to acetic acid, propionic acid, diacetyl. IR agonist criterion >=61 spikes/s (35% of best ligand). Calcium dF/F (Silbering 2011): acetic 23.1, propionic 21.4, diacetyl 23.3, butyric 5.9
receptor_specific.source: Silbering 2011; Prieto-Godino LL et al. 2016 Nature 539:93 doi:10.1038/nature19824

receptor_specific.facts: 1% ammonia standard stimulus causes adaptation; ammonia moderately attractive in T-maze

receptor_specific.empty_neuron: responses rise steeply 0.1% -> 100% CO2; ~half-maximal at 5%; low at ambient 0.035%

EC50_ESTIMATE.basis: native neuron more sensitive than empty-neuron (EC50 ~5%, Kwon 2007); behavior avoidance from +0.1% (Suh 2004, Faucher 2006) implies threshold ~0.05-0.1% above ambient. ESTIMATE

receptor_specific.source: Kwon JY et al. 2007 PNAS 104:3574 doi:10.1073/pnas.0700079104; Suh GS et al. 2004 Nature 431:854 doi:10.1038/nature02980; Faucher 2006 J Exp Biol 209:2739; Ai 2010

receptor_specific.facts: only ab4B/Or56a responds among >3000 odors (GC-SSR); DoOR ab4B consensus 0.57 (SFR-reset)
receptor_specific.EC50_UNVERIFIED: a search summary reported Hill n=0.27, log EC50=-11.1 (source unclear, low confidence)
receptor_specific.source: Stensmyr MC et al. 2012 Cell 151:1345 doi:10.1016/j.cell.2012.09.046

ORN_to_PN_transform.equation: PN = Rmax * ORN^1.5 / (ORN^1.5 + sigma^1.5 + (m*LFP)^1.5), LFP = sum(ORN rates over 24 types)/190
ORN_to_PN_transform.source: Olsen SR, Bhandawat V, Wilson RI 2010 Neuron 66:287, doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2010.04.009 (PMC2866644)

ORN_dynamics.adaptation: Weber-Fechner gain control at transduction; alpha=12.5/s, beta=1.26/s (Gorur-Shandilya 2017 model); adaptation within 500 ms
ORN_dynamics.intensity_invariance: normalized response dynamics invariant with concentration over most of dynamic range (Martelli 2013)
sources: Martelli C, Carlson JR, Emonet T 2013 J Neurosci 33:6285 doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.0426-12.2013
Nagel KI & Wilson RI 2011 Nat Neurosci 14:208 doi:10.1038/nn.2725
Gorur-Shandilya S, Demir M, Long J, Clark DA, Emonet T 2017 eLife 6:e27670

dilution_to_vapor_conversion_ESTIMATE.method: headspace partial pressure ~ mole fraction in solvent x Psat (Raoult, activity coefficient 1), then diluted by carrier stream
dilution_to_vapor_conversion_ESTIMATE.example: ethyl acetate 1e-2 v/v in paraffin oil (MW ~350) -> mole fraction ~0.04 -> ~0.5% (5000 ppm) headspace -> ~1000 ppm after Hallem 2006 1:5 carrier mixing (5.9 ml/s odor into 24 ml/s carrier)
dilution_to_vapor_conversion_ESTIMATE.rule_of_thumb: ppm_at_fly ~ dilution x (Psat_mmHg/760) x 1e6 x ~0.1-0.3 (for oil-diluted odorants; water-diluted polar compounds use Kaw)

delivery_conventions.Hallem2006: 5.9 ml/s odor stream into 24 ml/s carrier
delivery_conventions.Kreher2008: 3.75 ml/s into 37.5 ml/s; subtracted spontaneous AND solvent responses

gustatory._note: Tip-recording convention: spikes counted 0-500 ms after contact (x2 = spikes/s) with 30 mM tricholine citrate (TCC) electrolyte, which silences the water neuron (Charlu 2013; Dweck & Carlson 2020). Labellar sensilla: L-type strongest sugar responses; I-type ~1/3 of L; S-type good sucrose, weak other sugars (Hiroi 2002 Zool Sci 19:1009).

baseline_rates.source: Dweck HKM & Carlson JR 2023 Sci Adv doi:10.1126/sciadv.adj7032

sugar_GRNs.receptors: Gr5a (trehalose, glucose), Gr64a-f cluster (sucrose, maltose, fructose; Gr64f co-receptor; Gr64a not expressed in labellum), Gr61a; also Ir56b/Ir25a/Ir76b (low salt), Ir25a/Ir76b/Ir56d (fatty acids), Gr64e (glycerol)
sugar_GRNs.receptor_sources: Dahanukar A et al. 2007 Neuron 56:503 doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2007.10.024; Jiao Y et al. 2008 Curr Biol 18:1797 doi:10.1016/j.cub.2008.10.009; Fujii S et al. 2015 Curr Biol 25:621 doi:10.1016/j.cub.2014.12.058

data_points.source: Cameron P et al. 2010 Nature 465:91 doi:10.1038/nature09011
Dweck HKM et al. 2022 Curr Biol 32:1776 doi:10.1016/j.cub.2022.02.063

data_points.response: very few spikes (labellar L sensilla are poor fructose sensors)

data_points.source: Inagaki HK et al. 2012 Cell 148:583 doi:10.1016/j.cell.2011.12.022

hill_fit_sucrose_DERIVED.derivation: our 2-point fit of R = Rmax*C/(C+EC50) to 43 spikes/s @50 mM (Dweck 2022) and 59 @100 mM (Cameron 2010); different labs/sensilla, n fixed at 1. DERIVED ESTIMATE, consistent with saturation ~300-1000 mM.

glucose_EC50_mM_ESTIMATE.basis: glucose ~3-5x less potent than sucrose (Jiao 2008 qualitative). ESTIMATE

Gr43a_internal_fructose_sensor.brain_neuron_response: strong at 25 and 100 mM fructose, modest at 5 mM, none at 1 mM
Gr43a_internal_fructose_sensor.source: Miyamoto T, Slone J, Song X, Amrein H 2012 Cell 151:1113 doi:10.1016/j.cell.2012.10.024

sugar_GRNs.banana_relevance_DERIVED: ripe pulp juice ~370 mM glucose + ~360 mM fructose + ~90 mM sucrose (chemistry.json) -> sucrose-equivalent drive ~ saturating (R/Rmax ~0.8-0.9 with EC50s above). Taste discrimination ripe vs rotting therefore relies on acids, ethanol, yeast/amino acids, glycerol, not sugar level (rotting keeps ~13% hexose until yeast depletes it).

PER_behavior_sucrose.source: Inagaki HK, Panse KM, Anderson DJ 2014 Neuron 84:806 doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2014.09.032

other.source: Devineni AV et al. 2019 eLife 8:e47677 doi:10.7554/eLife.47677

bitter_GRNs.receptors: Gr66a, Gr33a, Gr32a, Gr39a, Gr89a, Gr93a (caffeine requires Gr66a & Gr93a); acids also activate bitter GRNs

data_points.behavior: still suppresses PER to 50 mM sucrose in starved flies

caffeine_EC50_mM_ESTIMATE.basis: responses routinely measured at 10 mM; Gr66a required (Moon SJ et al. 2006 Curr Biol 16:1812 doi:10.1016/j.cub.2006.07.024). ESTIMATE

tannin_polyphenol_ESTIMATE.model: weak Gr66a-class agonist; threshold ~0.1-1 mM catechin-equivalent
tannin_polyphenol_ESTIMATE.basis: no Drosophila GRN dose-response for tannic acid/banana polyphenols found. ESTIMATE
tannin_polyphenol_ESTIMATE.banana_relevance: ripe pulp tannin ~0.02 mg/g (~0.03 mM) -> sub-threshold; unripe pulp 0.66 mg/g (~1 mM) and peel ~0.2-0.5 mg/g -> near/above threshold (chemistry.json).

water_GRNs_ppk28.hypo_osmotic_activation: ppk28-expressing HEK cells respond to 216 and 174 mOsm/kg but not 236 (isotonic 303)

half_inhibition_osmolality_ESTIMATE_mOsm.basis: HEK data + 30 mM TCC (~90 mOsm) already suppresses firing in tip recordings. ESTIMATE

water_GRNs_ppk28.pharmacology: amiloride-sensitive (Chen Z, Wang Q, Wang Z 2010 J Neurosci 30:6247 doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.0627-10.2010)
water_GRNs_ppk28.banana_relevance: pulp juice osmolality ~1000+ mOsm (ESTIMATE) -> water GRNs silent on banana

behavior.source: Zhang YV, Ni J, Montell C 2013 Science 340:1334 doi:10.1126/science.1234133

tip_recordings.L4_low_salt: rises with NaCl, peaks at 100 mM, declines above
tip_recordings.S6_high_salt: rises from >=100 mM, max at 500 mM

cell_classes.low_salt_attractive: sweet GRNs (Na-specific, via Ir56b + Ir25a/Ir76b; Dweck 2022) + Ir94e neurons (weak response to 50 mM only)
cell_classes.high_salt_aversive: Gr66a bitter GRNs + ppk23-glutamatergic GRNs (both cation non-selective); Ir7c + Ir25a/Ir76b required in high-salt glut neurons (McDowell SAT et al. 2022 Curr Biol doi:10.1016/j.cub.2022.06.012)
cell_classes.source: Jaeger AH, Stanley M, Weiss ZF, Musso PY, Chan RC, Zhang H, Feldman-Kiss D, Gordon MD 2018 eLife 7:e37167 doi:10.7554/eLife.37167

data_points.response: activates all 9 L sensilla + S4, S8

data_points.stimulus: 50 mM sucrose + 50 mM NaCl in L1

salt.natural_note: fruit typically <=10 mM Na (Dweck 2022); banana ~0.6 mM Na, ~120 mM K (chemistry.json)

acids.bitter_GRN_activation: bitter neurons start firing at pH ~5 and increase with acidity (receptor-independent); acids inhibit sweet GRN responses depending on sugar:acid ratio (Charlu S, Wisotsky Z, Medina A, Dahanukar A 2013 Nat Commun 4:2042 doi:10.1038/ncomms3042)
acids.sugar_rescue: 10% citric acid rejected with 5 mM sucrose, acceptable with >=50 mM sucrose (Charlu 2013)

acetic_acid_two_choice_vs_2mM_sucrose.receptor: Ir7a in a bitter-GRN subset required for avoiding 5%
acetic_acid_two_choice_vs_2mM_sucrose.source: Rimal S et al. 2019 Cell Rep doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2019.01.042

other_acids_same_assay.lactic_acid: attractive 5%, slight preference 10%, neutral 15%, strongly aversive 20%

acids.lactic_acid_taste: activates sweet GRNs: onset via IR25a (lactate-specific), OFF response via Gr64a-f (low pH) (Stanley M, Ghosh B, Weiss ZF, Christiaanse J, Gordon MD 2021 Curr Biol doi:10.1016/j.cub.2021.06.005)
acids.OtopLA: proton channel for acid rejection; knockdown abolishes rejection of 50 uM-5 mM HCl (pH 4.4-2.4); 0.01 mM HCl mildly attractive, OtopLA-dependent (Ganguly A et al. 2021 PNAS 118:e2110641118 doi:10.1073/pnas.2110641118)
acids.tarsal_sour_GRNs: IR25a+IR76b; 100 mM acetic acid (pH 2.88) > 10 mM citric (pH 2.62) or 10 mM HCl (pH 2.0); no response at buffered pH >=5 (Chen Y & Amrein H 2017 Curr Biol 27:2741 doi:10.1016/j.cub.2017.08.003)

acetic_acid_GCaMP_Devineni2019.stimulus_is_undissociated_acid: HCl at same pH or K-acetate at same molarity gives no PER

acids.banana_relevance: rotting banana acetic acid ~0.05-1% (ESTIMATE, chemistry.json) sits in the indifferent-to-mildly-attractive taste range; vinegar-strength (5%) is aversive to taste in fed flies.

amino_acids_yeast.Ir76b_amino_acids: Ir76b required for yeast preference; amino acids tested at 25 mM vs 5 mM sucrose; preference increases up to 100 mM; leg Ir76b cells respond to serine 15-100 mM (Ganguly A et al. 2017 Cell Rep 18:737 doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2016.12.071)
amino_acids_yeast.labellar_sweet_GRN_amino_acids: Arg, Gly, Ala, Ser, Phe, Thr, Cys, Pro activate sweet GRNs (Gr5a/Gr61a/Gr64f + IR25a/IR76b); high Arg, Lys, Pro, Val, Trp, Ile, Leu activate bitter GRNs (biphasic) (Aryal B, Dhakal S, Shrestha B, Lee Y 2022 Curr Biol doi:10.1016/j.cub.2022.01.060)
amino_acids_yeast.taste_peg_yeast_GRNs: Ir76b/Ir25a taste-peg GRNs respond to 10% yeast more strongly than to 500 mM sucrose or water; amino-acid solutions give much smaller responses than yeast (Steck K et al. 2018 eLife 7:e31625 doi:10.7554/eLife.31625)

fatty_acids.hexanoic_acid: attraction plateaus ~1%, declines above (bitter recruitment); sweet GRN detection requires IR25a, IR76b, IR56d
fatty_acids.source: Ahn JE, Chen Y, Amrein H 2017 eLife 6:e30115 doi:10.7554/eLife.30115; Tauber JM et al. 2017 PLoS Genet 13:e1007059

glycerol.receptor: Gr64e in sweet GRNs (also pharyngeal PhG1); drives preference for yeast/beer
glycerol.source: Wisotsky Z, Medina A, Freeman E, Dahanukar A 2011 Nat Neurosci 14:1534 doi:10.1038/nn.2944

carbonation.cells: labellar taste-peg GRNs (E409-GAL4; claw taste pegs, IR56d per Tastekin 2025)
carbonation.source: Fischler W, Kong P, Marella S, Scott K 2007 Nature 448:1054 doi:10.1038/nature06101

ethanol_taste.PER: 0.1-40% ethanol never elicits PER and dose-dependently reduces PER to 100 mM sucrose (aversive taste)
ethanol_taste.consumption: flies nevertheless prefer 15% ethanol food in CAFE (5-25% increasing preference over days); internal ethanol 26-45 mM after starve-refeed, ~15 mM hyperactivity
ethanol_taste.source: Devineni AV & Heberlein U 2009 Curr Biol 19:2126 doi:10.1016/j.cub.2009.10.070

polyamines.behavior: mated females prefer 1 mM putrescine/cadaverine (~10 ppm, level in fermenting fruit); virgins only lowest levels
polyamines.source: Hussain A et al. 2016 PLoS Biol 14:e1002455 doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.1002455

hunger_sweet_bitter.effect: sugar sensitivity (PER dose-response shift), fed vs 2 d starved
bitter sensitivity decrease, fed vs 2 d starved

hunger_sweet_bitter.value: sugar sensitivity rises mostly within 6 h then slowly to 48 h; bitter sensitivity unchanged until >24 h
sweet: dopamine -> DopEcR in Gr5a GRNs (presynaptic enhancement); bitter: AKH -> sNPF+ neurosecretory cells -> GABA -> reduced Gr66a output

hunger_sweet_bitter.fold: 1.3-1.4x response to 400 mM sucrose with 1 mM bath dopamine; baseline 1.2x; starvation/L-dopa enhancement significant at 100 mM
hunger_sweet_bitter.note: DopEcR required at 6 h but not >=24 h starvation

hunger_sweet_bitter.value: ~1 Hz just fed -> ~25 Hz after 24 h starvation
hunger_sweet_bitter.source: Marella S, Mann K, Scott K 2012 Neuron 73:941 doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2011.12.032

hunger_sweet_bitter.value: starvation reduces tonic firing of octopaminergic OA-VL neurons; octopamine potentiates bitter GRN output -> starvation depotentiates bitter taste (no fold reported)
hunger_sweet_bitter.source: LeDue EE, Mann K, Koch E, Chu B, Dakin R, Gordon MD 2016 Curr Biol 26:2854 doi:10.1016/j.cub.2016.08.028

hunger_sweet_bitter.value: Devineni 2019 found no fed/starved difference in bitter GRN lobeline responses and only a trend (p=0.063) for sugar GRNs

acetic_acid_taste_switch.fed: 1-10% acetic acid PER ~ water (~20%); 10% acetic acid reduces 300 mM sucrose PER 79% -> 44%
acetic_acid_taste_switch.starved_2d: 86% PER to 10% acetic acid (76% without olfactory organs); acetic acid enhances PER to 5-10 mM sucrose; appears by 1 d, max at 2 d
acetic_acid_taste_switch.circuit: silencing Gr64f neurons in starved flies drops PER to 12-28%; silencing bitter neurons keeps >80% PER to sugar + 10% acetic acid
acetic_acid_taste_switch.source: Devineni AV, Sun B, Zhukovskaya A, Axel R 2019 eLife 8:e47677 doi:10.7554/eLife.47677

olfactory_first_synapse.paper: Root CM, Ko KI, Jafari A, Wang JW 2011 Cell 145:133 doi:10.1016/j.cell.2011.02.008
olfactory_first_synapse.findings: starvation increases DM1, DM4, DM2 responses to vinegar and decreases VM2, VA3; DM1 increase grows over first 4 h, no further at 12 h; sNPFR1 mRNA ~4x up in antennae; ectopic sNPFR1 in Or42b ORNs mimics starved food search
olfactory_first_synapse.stimuli: 0.1-0.4% saturated vapor cider vinegar; food finding ~60% at 25% vinegar

DM1_gain_fold_ESTIMATE.basis: figure only; not stated numerically. ESTIMATE

olfactory_first_synapse.paper: Ko KI, Root CM, Lindsay SA, ... Wang JW 2015 eLife 4:e08298 doi:10.7554/eLife.08298
olfactory_first_synapse.findings: DM5 (Or85a) activation threshold shifts from 20% saturated vapor vinegar (fed) to 80% (starved) = 4x threshold shift via tachykinin/DTKR (insulin-gated); DM1 at 80% SV unaffected (saturated)
olfactory_first_synapse.behavior: starved appetitive index (% reaching source in 10 min) 23 -> 60 over 0.5-25% vinegar, then declines; starved > fed at all concentrations 0.5-100%; sNPFR knockdown removes hunger effect at 0.5-1%, DTKR knockdown at 5-25%

olfactory_first_synapse.paper: Beshel J & Zhong Y 2013 J Neurosci doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.2605-13.2013
olfactory_first_synapse.findings: hunger increases food-odor (not non-food) responses in dNPF neurons in a graded way predicting attraction; no fold extracted

olfactory_first_synapse.paper: Sayin S et al. 2019 Neuron 104:544 doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2019.07.028
olfactory_first_synapse.findings: hungry flies persist in tracking food odor over repeated unrewarded trials; MBON->LH output + Dop1R2; octopaminergic VPM4 brakes persistence

CO2_state_dependence.paper: Braecker LB et al. 2013 Curr Biol 23:1228 doi:10.1016/j.cub.2013.05.029
CO2_state_dependence.findings: avoidance of CO2 >0.02% above ambient; in starved flies (or with food odor), avoidance requires MB and biVPN; starved flies partly suppress CO2 avoidance in presence of vinegar

CO2_state_dependence.paper: Lewis LPC et al. 2015 Curr Biol 25:2203 doi:10.1016/j.cub.2015.07.015
CO2_state_dependence.findings: food odor suppresses CO2 avoidance via MB beta'2 output neurons and PAM dopamine neurons (no magnitudes extracted)

CO2_state_dependence.paper: van Breugel F, Huda A, Dickinson MH 2018 Nature 564:420 doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0732-8
CO2_state_dependence.findings: CO2 attractive only in active/flying flies (IR25a-dependent, not Gr63a); aversive at low activity; 5% most effective of 1.7/5/15%; ethanol attractive in all states (2x search time vs CO2 or vinegar); rearing bottles 0.5-1% CO2

protein_mating_state.paper: Ribeiro C & Dickson BJ 2010 Curr Biol 20:1000 doi:10.1016/j.cub.2010.03.061
protein_mating_state.findings: mated, protein-deprived females prefer yeast; requires sex peptide receptor in ppk+ neurons and neuronal TOR/S6K

protein_mating_state.paper: Vargas MA, Luo N, Yamaguchi A, Kapahi P 2010 Curr Biol 20:1006 doi:10.1016/j.cub.2010.04.009
protein_mating_state.findings: mated females eat more yeast than virgins, females more than males (4% yeast extract vs 5% sucrose); S6K and serotonin; flies prefer the deprived nutrient

protein_mating_state.paper: Corrales-Carvajal VM, Faisal AA, Ribeiro C 2016 eLife 5:e19920 doi:10.7554/eLife.19920
protein_mating_state.findings: amino-acid deprivation increases yeast feeding 1.6x vs suboptimal diet; median latency to first long yeast visit 4.38 min (deprived) vs 12.37 min (suboptimal) = ~3x faster; Orco mutants ~25.6 min vs 5-8 min controls to start yeast exploitation
yeast taste GRN gain increases after 10 d yeast deprivation (n.s. at 3 d) and after 3 d amino-acid deprivation; sucrose responses unchanged; mating acts downstream of GRNs

protein_mating_state.paper: Walker SJ, Corrales-Carvajal VM, Ribeiro C 2015 Curr Biol 25:2621 doi:10.1016/j.cub.2015.08.043
protein_mating_state.findings: mating induces sex-peptide-dependent sodium appetite (more feeding initiation on salt), independent of need
mated females self-select P:C ~1:4 when given yeast vs sucrose; lifespan max at 1:16, egg-laying rate max at 1:2
mating shifts polyamine preference to 1 mM (Ir76b taste, Ir41a smell)

suggested_state_gains_for_model_ESTIMATE._note: Multiplicative gains relative to fed/virgin baseline, derived from the fold changes above. ESTIMATES for simulation defaults.

starved_24h.ORN_DM5_output_or_threshold: threshold x4 (i.e. gain ~0.25 at mid concentrations)

LB1a.evidence: FlyWire cell_sub_class bitter (FlyWire merges as "LB1a,LB1d"); Gr33a-GAL4 match (Tastekin); in Shiu neu_bitter

LB1b.evidence: FlyWire bitter; Gr33a match; Shiu neu_bitter (x3); FlyWire n=7

LB1c.evidence: FlyWire bitter; Gr33a match; Shiu neu_bitter (x9); FlyWire n=18; synapses directly onto Scapula (PER inhibition)

LB1d.evidence: as LB1a (merged in FlyWire, n=17 for LB1a,LB1d)

LB1e.modality: Ir94e (mildly aversive; glutamate/amino acids; weak low-salt response)
LB1e.evidence: Ir94e-GAL4 match (Tastekin); Shiu neu_ir94e = LB1e x11; FlyWire labels it bitter; Ir94e activation inhibits PER to 50 mM (not 1 M) sucrose (Shiu 2024); n=23

LB2a.evidence: FlyWire label "low-salt" derives from Engert 2022 NBLAST match to Ir94e only; Tastekin: no matching GAL4, aversive UMAP cluster; some Shiu Ir94e neurons fall here. FlyWire merges "LB2a-b" (n=8)
LB2a.warning: do NOT treat as attractive low-salt

LB2b.evidence: as LB2a; LB2b/LB2c output to GNG510 (aversive pathway)

LB2c.evidence: FlyWire "low-salt" (n=7); Tastekin aversive cluster; outputs GNG510

LB2d.modality: CONFLICT: FlyWire "sugar/water" (n=7, one in Shiu water set) vs Tastekin (MaleCNS-only, likely segmentation artifact)
LB2d.evidence: FlyWire LB2d shares partners with LB3 (CB0008/Usnea, AN_GNG_PRW_2) -> appetitive; may correspond to Tastekin LB4b (inference)

LB3.evidence: FlyWire sugar/water; Shiu neu_sugar = LB3 x20, neu_water = LB3 x17 (+LB2d x1); Shiu split sugar vs water by output connectivity (sugar -> G2N-1/FMIn; water -> Fudog/Phantom)

LB3d.modality: high salt / aversive (glutamatergic; Ir7c, ppk23, Ir47a)
LB3d.evidence: Ir7c-, ppk23-, Ir47a-GAL4 match; described as aversive heavy-metal/high-salt sensing (Tastekin); outputs overlap appetitive partners (may inhibit attraction)

LB4a.evidence: Tastekin: novel type in attractive cluster (partners AN27X021, PRW047); FlyWire "low-salt" (n=4); top FlyWire partners AN_GNG_PRW_2, CB0883, CB0902, DNg103 shared with PhG1 (Gr64e, appetitive)

claw_tpGRN.evidence: Ir56d-GAL4 and Gr64e-GAL4 match; carbonation sensing via IR56d (Tastekin and cited prior work); own UMAP cluster with LgAG6; FlyWire n=60

dorsal_tpGRN.modality: amino acid / yeast (feeding-burst prolongation in AA-deprived flies)
dorsal_tpGRN.evidence: Gr5a-GAL4 and Ir60d-GAL4 match; companion work shows dtpGRN prolongs yeast feeding bursts under AA deprivation; FlyWire n=11. Steck 2018 Ir76b/Ir25a peg neurons not resolved to claw vs dorsal

PhG2.modality: unknown, probably aversive (drives GNG055 -> inhibits Fdg; top FlyWire partner CB0498 43%)

PhG3.modality: water (ppk28-GAL4 match; but in aversive UMAP cluster)

PhG12.modality: unknown, probably aversive (clusters with LgAG4/7/9, shares GNG016)

PhG13.modality: Ir67c, aversive cluster (possibly sexually dimorphic outputs; pheromone-taste link)

leg_ascending_LgAG._note: FlyWire has these as SA_VTV_1-5, 7-10; exact SA_VTV_n <-> LgAG_n correspondence not obtained. Partner-overlap inference: SA_VTV_1 and SA_VTV_5 aversive (CB0159/CB0219), SA_VTV_2 appetitive (AN_GNG_PRW_2, DNg103) -- low confidence.

LgAG1.evidence: Gr33a-GAL4 match; partners TPN3, AN05B023a (inhibits PPN1); all 6 legs

LgAG2.evidence: Gr61a-GAL4 match; attractive cluster; all 6 legs

LgAG9.modality: unknown, probably aversive (GNG016, GNG510; 1 neuron in FlyWire)

LgLG4.modality: sugar + low salt (Gr64f, Ir56b; partners Dandelion, DNg103)

LgLG5.modality: male-specific pheromone (ppk23+/ppk25+, glutamatergic; foreleg -> T1 contralateral)

second_order_neurons._note: Nickname = FlyWire v783 cell_type. Output percentages computed from Shiu 2024 Connectivity_783 joined to FlyWire annotations (our computation).

water.Zorro: (named in Shiu 2024; FlyWire type not mapped)
water.note: >half (250) of activated neurons shared between sugar and water pathways (Shiu 2024)

bitter.dominant_shared_partner: CB0159 (GABA): 28% of LB1b, 25% LB1e, 16% LB1c, 26% PhG16, 21% SA_VTV_5 outputs; likely = GNG016 (feedback onto aversive GRNs) -- inference, unverified
bitter.aversive_chain_Tastekin: GNG016 -> GNG510 -> GNG087 (Scapula, inhibits PER) and GNG088 (GABA, inhibits pharyngeal pumping MNs); LB1c -> Scapula directly; PhG2 and LB1c -> GNG055 -| Fdg (GNG588 MaleCNS = CB0038 FlyWire)

main_uncertainties: FlyWire "low-salt" on LB2a-b, LB2c, LB4a conflicts with Tastekin (LB2 aversive/unknown, LB4 appetitive/unknown) and Shiu Ir94e results; treat as morphology-only
Attractive low-salt is most likely carried by sugar GRNs themselves (Ir56b in LB3b, LgLG4); no separate low-salt type in FlyWire
FlyWire LB3 not split into LB3a-d; sugar/water/high-salt subtypes only via MaleCNS names or partner-based splitting
PhG modalities rest on single GAL4 matches; valence from UMAP clustering, not physiology

biggest_gaps: No published EC50/Hill fits extracted for adult Or42b-ethyl acetate, Or92a-diacetyl, Ir64a/Ir75a-acetic acid (figure-only or absent); defaults are estimates.
Dilution-to-vapor (ppm) conversion for DoOR/Hallem data is approximate (+/- 1 log unit).
Sugar GRN EC50s (sucrose/glucose/fructose) not tabulated in accessible text; sucrose fit is 2-point derived.
No Drosophila taste data for tannins/banana polyphenols; no in vivo osmolality curve for ppk28; no glycerol/carbonation dose-responses.
Starvation fold-change of DM1 ORN output (Root 2011) and yeast-GRN gain (Steck 2018) not stated numerically.
Conflicting reports on whether hunger changes bitter GRN output (Inagaki 2014/LeDue 2016 vs Devineni 2019).
Several FlyWire GRN types (LB2, LB4, most PhG, LgAG3-9) have unknown or inferred modality.
